articles.title: Download now
articles.description: Top stories, breaking news, live reporting, and follow news topics that match your interests

articles.title: Mexico Investigates Possible Cartel Links of Prosecutor Who Aided C.I.A.
articles.description: The prosecutor recently fled to the United States after Mexico issued a warrant over his involvement with the C.I.A. Now authorities are investigating him for suspected cartel collusion.

articles.title: Gordon Ramsay to Host Revival of BBC’s ‘Top Gear’
articles.description: The British car show “Top Gear” paused production three years ago and is returning with a new host in 2028, the BBC said.

articles.title: Lukoil to Sell Foreign Assets, but Not to Kushner and Witkoff Associates
articles.description: Valuable properties belonging to the Russian energy giant will be sold to an American-led consortium. But Middle Eastern business contacts of the two Trump envoys pulled out because of political winds.

articles.title: Road Fire Near Cairo Kills Dozens After Petroleum-Laden Truck Crashes
articles.description: The blaze killed at least 31 and injured at least 21 near Giza, beside the Nile River, officials said.

articles.title: Island Paradise of Mauritius Has Sun, Beaches and Too Many Dogs
articles.description: Mauritius, a popular tourist destination off southern Africa, has become overrun with strays. With more and more residents chased and attacked, many are fed up.

articles.title: Libyan Forces Threaten Retaliation Over Ukraine’s Attack on Russian Ships
articles.description: The Ukrainian drone strike off Libya’s coast killed two Libyan naval officers, according to the forces controlling the country’s east.

articles.title: Opposition Makes Progress Toward Ousting Netanyahu, Party Leader Says
articles.description: Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief, has set Dec. 6 as the deadline to form a new Israeli government. His ally, Avigdor Liberman, said Mr. Eisenkot was on track.

articles.title: 2 Men Charged After Break-In at Prince William and Kate’s Country Home
articles.description: Prosecutors said the two men, who appeared in court on Wednesday, had climbed a drainpipe to break into the royals’ country retreat in Norfolk.

articles.title: North Korea Kicks Out Swiss Diplomats in Spat Linked to Ukraine War
articles.description: The move followed Switzerland’s decision to impose sanctions on an international youth camp in North Korea, which is accused of hosting Ukrainian children for indoctrination.

articles.title: South African President Wins Reprieve From ‘Farmgate’ Impeachment Investigation
articles.description: A court threw out a report suggesting that Cyril Ramaphosa may have tried to conceal the theft of more than half a million dollars of U.S. currency.

articles.title: How an Iranian Ally Gained the Upper Hand in Yemen’s War
articles.description: The Iran-backed Houthis are on a winning streak, securing strategic territory as they fight Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies in an asymmetrical war of attrition.

articles.title: Defending Aden, Yemen’s Holdout Against the Houthis
articles.description: The war in Iran has reignited Yemen’s decade-old civil war. Saudi-backed troops are scrambling to defend against advancing Houthi fighters as the wounded are taken to the port city of Aden, the government’s provisional capital.

articles.title: Colombia’s Leader Blames ‘Terrorist Attack’ for Power Outages
articles.description: The blackouts follow a string of violent episodes attributed to Colombia’s armed traffickers, as the country’s new president cracks down on the groups.

articles.title: Jilted bride who went ahead with her wedding alone finally walks down the aisle
articles.description: Guests burst into applause as Swansea bride Kayley Stead, jilted in 2022, finally says "I do".

articles.title: Hungary Threw Open Its Secret Police Files. Let the Finger Pointing Begin.
articles.description: The communist-era files have exposed the vast network of informants that kept Hungary in the Soviet orbit. But how reliable are they?

articles.title: U.K. Releases Files on Peter Mandelson, Ambassador Tied to Jeffrey Epstein
articles.description: Documents released Thursday shed new light on the rushed appointment of Peter Mandelson and his continued ties to Global Counsel, a lobbying group.

articles.title: Ontario Premier Says He’d Use a Gun to Protect His Family
articles.description: Recent home invasions have stirred unease in Toronto. On Thursday, the premier of Ontario said he would fire a gun in self-defense ‘in a heartbeat.’

articles.title: Judges in Israel Suggest Dropping Key Corruption Case Against Netanyahu
articles.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is accused of bribery, fraud and breach of trust in a long-running trial that has divided the country. He denies all wrongdoing.

articles.title: Two Italians Killed in Iranian Drone Attack on Kuwait, Officials Say
articles.description: The deaths follow a series of strikes on Gulf Arab states that host U.S. military facilities in recent weeks as talks to end the war continue to stall.

articles.title: Net Migration to U.K. Falls to Lowest Level Since 1997, Excluding Pandemic
articles.description: The drop was largely driven by fewer people arriving from outside the European Union. It reflects government action to restrict immigration after a public backlash.

articles.title: After Cyberattacks and Bomb Threats Hit Europe, Survivalism Goes Mainstream
articles.description: More governments in Europe are telling citizens to prepare for emergencies. After unexpected disruptions, many are listening.

articles.title: The Unbearable Heat of Delhi’s Summer Nights
articles.description: Residents of India’s dense capital tried switching off fridges and leaving doors open all night to cope with rising temperatures, which affect their sleep, health and ability to work.

articles.title: Brazilian Duped Into Fighting for Russia: ‘War Is Hell’
articles.description: Dozens of Brazilians have joined the Russian army, some say lured by a pair of recruiters promising money and adventure. Here is one soldier’s story.

articles.title: 13 Dead and 13 Thought Trapped in Indonesian Mine After Heavy Rain
articles.description: Dozens of workers had been stuck inside the illegal gold mine since Monday, after its narrow shafts flooded. Rescuers said they were losing hope that those still inside would be found alive.

articles.title: Gérard Depardieu Is Ordered to Stand Trial Over Rape Accusation
articles.description: The actress Charlotte Arnould has accused the French movie star of raping her in 2018. He has denied any wrongdoing in the case.

articles.title: Lured by High Salaries, Some Brazilians Were Duped Into Fighting for Russia
articles.description: Dozens of Brazilians were sent to the front lines with little training, and the high salaries they were promised, they say, turned out to be illusory.

articles.title: Attack Blamed on ISIS Kills 2 Syrian Security Force Members
articles.description: The assault on a security headquarters in the northeastern city of Hasakah was carried out by four militants who local officials linked to the Islamic State.

articles.title: El Salvador’s Nayib Bukele Elates Haiti With Fight Against Gangs
articles.description: The president of El Salvador has widespread support among Haitians, who are tired of violence and hope he can be the one to finally end it.

articles.title: The E.R. Closed at 5 P.M. A Dying Woman Showed Up 11 Minutes Too Late.
articles.description: In rural British Columbia, Courtney McCowan died after paramedics tried to help her in a hospital’s parking lot.

articles.title: How Birds With GPS and Audio Sensors Track Hidden Fishing Boats
articles.description: Researchers are using seabirds equipped with GPS and audio gear to detect vessels that operate with no tracking signals and to assess the environmental hazards they pose.

articles.title: Alaskan flying team airdrops Thanksgiving turkeys to remote communities
articles.description: For the last few years, the "turkey bombers" have taken to the skies for the benefit of residents in off-grid communities.

articles.title: Was Japan Prime Minister Takaichi Snubbed at China’s Big Summit?
articles.description: Images show the differences between the welcomes afforded to Sanae Takaichi and other world leaders in Shenzhen, as some officials in Japan cry foul.

articles.title: Hong Kong Grieves Fire Victims Under Watchful Eye of Authorities
articles.description: The city’s residents quietly mourned the 168 lives lost in a high-rise complex blaze a year ago, as officials warned against using the disaster to sow division.

articles.title: Study Hard, Get Ahead?
articles.description: The broken promise of upward mobility through education is sparking youth protests around the world.

articles.title: Bellingham's backing of reporter praised after viral clip
articles.description: A clip of Jude Bellingham preventing someone from interrupting a reporter has gone viral.

articles.title: London Banning Noise and Capping Fares for Its Pedicabs
articles.description: Starting Friday, the city will regulate pedicab operators for the first time, imposing fare caps and noise restrictions.

articles.title: An Italian Couple Bought a House Built by Pier Paolo Pasolini. Local Villagers Want to Evict Them.
articles.description: After an Italian couple bought a house built by Pier Paolo Pasolini, one of the country’s greatest film directors, local villagers claimed the property.

articles.title: How to Celebrate Thanksgiving as an Expat
articles.description: From turkeys delivered on motorbikes to foie gras on the table, many American expatriates have adapted the traditional meal to their environs.

articles.title: Africa C.D.C. Chief Faces Turmoil Over Management Amid Ebola Crisis
articles.description: Scrutiny has fallen on Dr. Jean Kaseya, the director general of the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, after reports of staff intimidation and mismanagement of funds.

articles.title: Two staff killed in Israeli strike on Gaza medical clinic, MSF says
articles.description: The Israeli military says it targeted "Hamas terrorists" in the strike which has been condemned by the World Health Organization.

articles.title: Actor and comedian PJ Gallagher dies aged 51
articles.description: PJ Gallagher appeared on Irish television for more than two decades with shows including Naked Camera and The Young Offenders.

articles.title: Seven students killed and nearly 100 injured in explosion in Afghanistan, official says
articles.description: A spokesman for Afghanistan's interior ministry says the blast was caused by carelessness at an explosives depot nearby.

articles.title: Ukraine’s Deep Strikes Grow in Scale and Scope Across Russia and Beyond
articles.description: A campaign aimed at depriving Moscow’s war machine of fuel, weapons and money has been criticized by the Trump administration.

articles.title: Canada’s Arctic Reservists Know the Land. Fewer Young People Do.
articles.description: Canada relies on Inuit and First Nations Rangers’ traditional knowledge of the land to protect its most inhospitable corners. But that knowledge is disappearing.

articles.title: Freed From a Notorious Syrian Prison, but Still Trapped by Its Terror
articles.description: Ahmed al-Shalh expected to perish in Sednaya prison. Abruptly released after a decade, he reveled in marriage and fatherhood but struggled to shake his ghosts.

articles.title: 'I was trying to be someone I wasn't' – Steward on All Blacks shot
articles.description: Freddie Steward says he has previously been distracted by comparisons with different sorts of players on previous England starts.

articles.title: Pensions and benefits services still down after 'cyber incident'
articles.description: The UK's former chief technology officer says the Department for Work and Pensions may have been hit by hackers, but the government has not confirmed that.

articles.title: Princess Catherine’s Cancer Documentary ‘Heal’: 3 Takeaways
articles.description: ‘Heal,’ a 30-minute authorized documentary released this week, offers glimpses into Catherine’s recovery since her 2024 cancer diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: Set time aside for children to read for pleasure, schools to be told
articles.description: The government says its new cirriculum hopes to reverse declining literacy rates and combat "mindless scrolling".
